items.q: Should each of the seven gigs get its own keynote?
items.a: No. **One keynote**, addressed to the room. A **15-minute** version can stretch to an hour. Custom talks throw away the dial-in.

items.q: What does he spend so the paid hour also makes clips?
items.a: About **$500** for a hired videographer in that city. A **real camera**, a second camera, and AV. Not an iPhone on a tripod.

items.q: Where do the best clips come from if the talk never changes?
items.a: From **Q&A**. On a **60-minute** slot, speak about **45** and take **three questions**.

items.q: Why take the slot before lunch?
items.a: Then you can stand in the **hallway** and invite people to say hello. He says his early vlog clips came from those questions.

items.q: What is the gift on a normal stage?
items.a: Something already on screen, a **PDF or the slides**. **Follow on Instagram** and message a keyword. He skipped it on his wife's Pink Skirt stage.

items.q: How much of the money is after the fee?
items.a: He says most speakers make **three to four times** more on the back end. A **$10K** fee could become **$40K to $50K**. Reinvest that in media.

items.q: What fee ladder does he name for himself?
items.a: Free, then travel, then **$5K**, **$10K**, **$25K** after the book, **$50K** near a million followers, **$100K** from 2 million to 10 million. Then **deliver the goods**.
